# Babysit PR

Many repos have AI review bots. They're helpful, even if they are not always
right.

## Waiting

Never write your own watcher, polling loop, or `sleep` loop. Use one watcher
per PR: `watch_pull_request` in T3 Code, `pr-wait` everywhere else. Never run
both on the same PR. Every watcher on a GitHub account shares one rate limit.

### In T3 Code: `watch_pull_request`

Handle the existing checks and comments first. Then call
`watch_pull_request` and end your turn. T3 Code wakes you with a message when
a check fails, the required checks pass, someone comments or reviews, or the
branch conflicts.

- **Only the thread that owns the PR watches it.** If you are a delegated
  child task (a reviewer, a Sol round, any `delegate_task` child), never call
  `watch_pull_request`. The parent owns the PR. Do not watch PRs you are not
  working on.
- **A wake is news, not a merge decision.** Check the merge gate yourself.
- **Unwatch when you hand off.** A watched thread stays in Working and out of
  the user's inbox. When you stop (ready, blocked, or asking the user a question),
  call `unwatch_pull_request` first. A merge or close ends the watch on its
  own.
- **"Stopped watching, could not read it"** usually means GitHub's rate limit
  is used up. Run `gh api rate_limit --jq .resources.graphql` before you
  watch again. If `remaining` is near 0, wait for `reset` with one background
  command, then watch again. Never watch again in a tight loop.

### Everywhere else: `pr-wait`

Wait with `scripts/pr-wait` from this skill's directory (use its absolute
path).

```bash
pr-wait <pr> [--repo owner/name] [--until ready|green|any-change]
```

It prints one line per real event. It exits 0 when the `--until` condition is
met or the PR merges, 1 when it needs you (a required check failed, conflicts,
unresolved threads, PR closed), and 2 on bad input.

- `ready` (default): required checks green, Greptile or Macroscope reviewed the
  head, and no unresolved threads. Use this to babysit.
- `green`: required checks only. Use it when the repo has no Greptile or
  Macroscope.
- `any-change`: exit on the first event.

In Claude Code, run it with the Monitor tool (`timeout_ms: 3600000`), so each
line wakes you. Without a monitor, run it as one long command. It ends on its
own.

Start it again after you push, after you handle an exit 1, and after a resume.
It remembers what it already reported, so nothing that arrived in between is
lost. If it says another pid already watches the PR, do not start a second one.
Kill the old one only if its events do not reach you.

With either watcher: when an event needs no action, end your turn without a
message. Never post or say "still waiting".

## GitHub rate limits

`gh pr create`, `gh pr view`, and `gh pr checks` use GraphQL. When GraphQL is
used up, the REST limit is separate and usually still has room. Use
`gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/pulls/<n>` to read a PR, and
`gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/commits/<sha>/check-runs` for checks.

## Reviews

Only act on checks and comments newer than the latest push. Verify every bot
finding against the source before changing code. Fix real findings and CI
failures, distinguish repository failures from infrastructure flakes, and reply
with a written reason when dismissing false positives.

If the repo has `.macroscope/check-run-agents/*.md`, read those rules before you
reply to a Macroscope finding. Its findings cite them.

CodeRabbit is advisory. Treat its findings like any other finding, but never
wait for it and never hold a merge for it.

If a review bot leaves feedback you believe is not worth addressing, reply with
a written reason and resolve the comment. Use the `leaving-pr-comments` skill
for every comment posted on the user's behalf.

Screenshots and videos help as well, when you have a way to upload them.

Keep the PR at the size the user's goal needs. Review loops tend to grow a
PR one cheap-looking fix at a time. Fix real bugs in the intended case.
Decline the rest with a written reason, and list them as follow-ups:
unneeded tests, guards for edge cases that do not matter, extra integration
or compatibility, and small performance costs. Prefer the fix that deletes or
narrows code.

## Base branch and merging

Keep an eye on changes to `main` and rebase when needed. `pr-wait` reports when
new base commits touch this PR's files, and when the PR becomes BEHIND or DIRTY.
`watch_pull_request` reports conflicts only, so check for BEHIND yourself
before you call the PR ready.
If an overlapping PR makes this one obsolete, stop monitoring, report it to the
user, and ask before closing the PR unless closure was explicitly authorized.

If nothing has changed, stay quiet rather than posting filler comments. Stop
when `pr-wait` exits 0, or in T3 Code when the merge gate passes on the latest
head. Merge only when the user explicitly requested it;
otherwise report that the PR is ready. Right before a merge, run `git fetch` and
check the PR again. Never merge when it is BEHIND or DIRTY, or when base commits
that landed after the last green run touch this PR's files. Rebase, push, and
wait for green again.
# Five-PR delivery stacks

The current user policy is to accumulate five dependent PRs before integrating the
batch into master. Keep each layer coherent and reviewable. Assemble five layers
before the final combined merge to master.

```text
master ← PR1 ← PR2 ← PR3 ← PR4 ← PR5
```

The bottom PR targets master. Each later PR targets the preceding layer's branch,
so its review shows that layer's change. Use `stack/<batch>-<layer>-<description>`

While an earlier layer runs CI, build the next dependent layer when its scope is

Stacking alone does not suppress preview builds. `vercel.json` sets

Unspecified branches retain their normal behavior, including master. Keeping every

See [Vercel's Git configuration](https://vercel.com/docs/project-configuration/git-configuration).
Do not add a broad true rule overlapping `stack/**`: Vercel deploys when any matching

# Classic release closeout

On 2026-11-14 the user chose this finish line: **faithful release: fix visible and
gameplay bugs, verify a full playthrough, and document remaining rare differences**.
The classic stays available for playing and experimentation. Modernization,
rebranding and new platform features are separate work.

The [fidelity ledger](fidelity.md) and [fixed seven-package checklist](completion-checklist.md)
retain their stricter original-comparison criteria. Open parity checkpoints are
not silently completed by this release decision. They describe the remaining
comparison work and known limits; closing every one is no longer a prerequisite
to the user-selected classic release.

## Release gates

1. The combined artwork stack is delivered through the authorized single master merge after current-head quick PR checks and review inspection.
2. The resulting master build passes the complete applicable offline browser suite, formatting, TypeScript and rule checks. Missing supplied-file cases are explicit; source-file coverage is verified locally.
3. A recorded supplied-art complete progression route verifies earned upgrades through boss defeat, the win screen and Continue. The full accelerated browser pilot is the release's progression integration test. Ordinary public-page checks retain their separate scope: a partial ordinary-input run is not described as a full normal-time playthrough.
4. Visible/gameplay defects found in release acceptance are fixed and affected checks pass. Concrete release blockers take priority over further edge-case instrumentation.
5. Original and mock asset entry, creator/library/save/code routes, controls, pause/settings and local progression are usable. Actual browser audio output and mute controls are checked; decoded buffers and muted headless callbacks alone do not satisfy that check. Subjective/synchronized original-audio comparison remains disclosed.
6. Player-facing run/file instructions and the remaining-differences record agree with the shipped build. No SWF, extracted media or dependency/build output is committed. Retired online services stay disabled.

A successful PR smoke permits merging under the user's revised CI policy; the
full master run is still a release gate. See [delivery](delivery.md) for the exact
commands and post-merge budget. A release is not claimed while these gates remain
open. [Classic validation](classic-validation.md) records the evidence and its
scope. These are criteria, not a live checkbox counter: the final `classic-v1`
annotated tag is created only after the resulting master full-suite gate passes,
and records its exact commit and CI run. It preserves the classic source while
modernization proceeds separately.

## Differences to disclose at release

The complete technical evidence remains in the fidelity ledger. The player-facing
release notes must identify applicable remaining differences, including:

- Mock paint and synthesized audio are approximations of the supplied artwork/audio.
- Exact antialiasing, filters/device fonts and some menu/transition pixels differ.
- Complete physical World sibling order, unusual overlapping/replaced fields and
  some constructor/event/Timer/RNG edges are not fully qualified.
- Remaining advanced-part/collision, audio synchronization and medal edge
  comparisons have bounded evidence rather than complete Adobe/runtime parity.
- Retired community/accounts/sharing/parts-pack/portal services are omitted;
  documented offline tools and usability additions retain their existing scope.

These are disclosure categories, not permission to leave a demonstrated ordinary
play defect unresolved. New observations should distinguish reproducible game
failures from test-tool errors and incomplete observations.

# Open Bubble Tank

A modular TypeScript reconstruction of **Bubble Tanks 3**, built with **Bun, Next.js, Tailwind CSS, and PixiJS**. The implementation uses the recovered game rules and data in the sibling [`documented-bubble-tank-3`](../documented-bubble-tank-3) repository.

**The one-to-one recreation is still in progress.** This repository contains a playable offline implementation, not a claim of completed pixel or behavioral parity. The remaining differences are tracked in [the fidelity ledger](docs/fidelity.md). Continuation starts with [the handoff](docs/handoff.md) and [the goal objective](goals.markdown).

This is the classic offline version. Its selected
[faithful-release criteria](docs/classic-release.md) cover the complete progression
route, concrete player-visible problems and documented remaining differences.
[Validation and its limits](docs/classic-validation.md) distinguish the accelerated
full progression test from ordinary public-input checks. Modernization and
rebranding are separate work.
Once the final master checks pass, the `classic-v1` tag preserves the accepted
classic source independently of later modernization.

## Run

Requires Bun 1.3.9+ and Node.js 20.9+ (Next.js tooling).

```sh
bun install
bun run dev
```

Open [localhost:3000](http://localhost:3000). Choose your Bubble Tanks 3 `.swf` at the asset screen, or choose **Play with mock assets**. The original game file and artwork are not bundled. Everything is extracted on the device: there is no upload endpoint, Flash player, or execution of ActionScript.

To obtain the game file yourself, open [Bubble Tanks 3 on Internet Archive](https://archive.org/details/bubble-tanks-3). Under **Download Options**, choose **SHOCKWAVE FLASH**, then select the downloaded `.swf` in the game. The asset screen includes the same guide. Mock mode supplies synthesized sound effects and quiet looping tones, translucent bubble bodies, yellow/orange weapons, and procedural projectiles with authored sizes and source-derived colors.

Normal compressed CWS and uncompressed FWS containers are supported. The research repository's already-expanded SWF with a retained CWS header is also recognized after checking its stage dimensions and frame rate. ZWS/LZMA is unsupported.

```sh
bun run check         # TypeScript and deterministic simulation/data tests
bun run format:check  # Formatting
bun run test:e2e      # Production build + Chrome/Playwright browser flows
bun run test:e2e:smoke # Quick PR browser flow, including the production build
bun run test:e2e:offline # Full mock/synthetic suite used on master
bun run build
bun run start
bun run fixtures      # Gameplay/art/screen fixtures on localhost:3102
```

The browser tests use Chrome if installed, otherwise a Playwright Chromium installation. To install Chromium, run `bun x playwright install chromium`. SWF integration tests use `BT3_SWF_FILE` or the sibling research fixture, and skip when neither exists. No SWF is committed to this project.

Playwright's disposable per-test output is isolated in `test-results/playwright`.
Keep independent validation records in ignored `reference-captures/` directories;
the runner must not use their parent as its output directory.

PR CI runs formatting, TypeScript/rules, a production build and the quick mock
startup/creator/settings/exploration/pause flow. Master pushes and manual CI runs
retain the full mock/synthetic browser suite, including the progression pilot.
The long post-merge pilot has a larger hosted wall-clock budget; its inputs,
simulation cap and earned upgrade/boss/win assertions stay the same. See
[delivery](docs/delivery.md) and the [classic release gates](docs/classic-release.md).

Ordinary navigation tests use `e2e/helpers/main-menu.ts` to wait for the native title intro before selecting a menu control. The title's hit geometry can cover an otherwise visible button. Controlled menu fixtures test input during the intro and on animated hover edges separately.

The repeatable metadata importers read the sibling research checkout without copying artwork:

```sh
python3 tools/import-reference-data.py --parts-only # Catalog strings, costs and stable IDs
bun tools/import-creator-controls.ts               # Creator controls and transforms
bun tools/import-creator-palette.ts                # Palette, stats and rollover layouts
bun tools/import-creator-dialogs.ts                # Save/exit/code screen layouts
bun tools/import-tank-viewer.ts                    # Local viewer, sorting and detail layouts
```

Part strings are decoded directly from the recovered ActionScript table, including quoted flavor text. Generated JSON is committed; the research checkout is needed only when regenerating it.

## Original runtime reference

The development reference viewer runs the supplied SWF with pinned Ruffle 0.7.1. It is separate from the game application and is excluded from the production bundle. It normalizes the research file's expanded CWS header to FWS and blocks retired external requests. Ruffle is an emulator, so observed differences still need to be checked against the recovered code.

Run `bun run reference` in one terminal and `bun run reference:browser` in another. The latter starts an owned headless Chrome with a larger WASM stack; default Chrome's stack overflows on this SWF.
